title: Fix a hook tight to a hollow panel with its toggle bolt
instruction: Fix the hook tight against the panel, square to the pencil line.
context: General maintenance and repair workers (about 1.5 million in the US) hang hooks, brackets and fixtures on hollow walls with spring-wing toggle bolts. The usual way this job fails is the toggle spinning in the cavity: the nut behind the board cannot be reached, and the only thing that stops it is pulling the fixture outward, and keeping it pulled while the screw turns, so the wings bite on the back of the board. That pull-to-hold is the skill tested here.
setup: Positions from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the midline halfway between them, heights are above the table top. Panel (fixed, lying face-up): a hollow wall section 25 cm front to back and 30 cm wide, centred 30.0 cm in front on the midline: a wooden 2x3 frame (four studs 38 mm thick and 63.5 mm deep round the edge) under grey 12.7 mm wallboard, so the board's face is 76.2 mm above the table and the closed cavity under it is 63.5 mm deep with no access. A prepared hole 12.7 mm across goes through the board 30.0 cm in front and 3.5 cm right. A pencil line 3 mm wide runs left-right across the face through the hole's centre. Hook (loose, steel, 150 g): a flat plate 40 mm front to back, 125 mm long and 3 mm thick lying on the face along the pencil line, its right end 40 mm right of the hole; 80 mm left of the hole an upright 5 mm thick (front to back), 24 mm wide and 32 mm tall stands on it, with a lip at its top running 16 mm further left and turning up 10 mm. Toggle bolt: a 3/16 in (10-24) x 2-1/2 in machine screw (4.8 mm, 1.06 mm per turn) with a zinc mushroom head 12 mm across and 4.6 mm tall and a cross recess (slots 2.6 mm wide, 3 mm deep), through the plate and the hole. On it in the cavity, the spring-wing toggle nut with its wings opened: 48 mm across, 11 mm wide and 6 mm thick, lying front-back, its upper face 3 mm below the board's back face (about 2.8 turns of thread to take up). Screwdriver (loose, 90 g): a stubby ratcheting #2 Phillips, 92 mm long: red handle 35 mm across and 50 mm long with a black cap, a 6 mm shaft 35 mm long and a cross tip of two blades 5.5 x 1.2 x 3 mm. The ratchet drives clockwise (seen from above) and freewheels anticlockwise. It stands tip-down in a holder: a fixed black block 50 x 50 x 45 mm centred 30.0 cm in front and 21.5 cm right, with a 14 mm vertical bore through it; the handle rests on the block's top. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, with both grippers more than 5 mm from the hook, the screwdriver (put down or still in a hand) at least 5 mm from it, and the hook at rest for the last 1 s. Tight: every corner of the hook plate's underside within 0.5 mm of the board face, and the toggle's wings within 0.5 mm of the board's back face (no gap left on the thread). Square: the plate's long axis within 3 degrees of the pencil line, with the hook end still to the left of the hole. 1.0: tight and square. 0.5: tight with the plate 3 to 10 degrees off the line. 0 otherwise: loose or part-tightened (the toggle spun with the screw, or the plate is held off the face), more than 10 degrees off, turned round, a gripper within 5 mm or the screwdriver closer than 5 mm, or the hook moving. Judged over the whole trial: if the toggle is ever unscrewed off the end of the bolt (lost in the cavity), the trial scores 0.
reset_notes: 1. Unscrew the bolt (anticlockwise) until the wings are 3 mm below the board's back face, about 2.8 turns from tight; the toggle spins unless the hook is pulled out while turning, so hold the hook up off the face while unscrewing. 2. Lay the hook plate flat on the face along the pencil line, hook end to the left, the wings lying front-back. 3. Stand the screwdriver tip-down in its holder's bore. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: True size. Simplified: the panel lies face-up on the bench so a straight-down tool can turn the screw; on a wall the same pull-and-turn is needed. The thread is an ideal 1.06 mm/turn helical joint with drag in place of thread friction; the toggle starts opened behind the board with about 2.8 turns left; the recess has square-sided slots; the ratchet pawl is a moving joint limit; the board is slightly springy. Fixed layout: a memorised replay cannot be ruled out.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right arm reached toward the screwdriver and stopped; the hook was not touched); demo: 1.0
